key_insight: A label-free physics-informed neural network can approximate spatially variable slope stability under non-associated Mohr-Coulomb plasticity, and a neural operator can then emulate reliability outputs for millions of random fields quickly.
engineering_relevance: This offers a fast surrogate workflow for slope reliability analysis that preserves failure mechanisms and factor-of-safety trends closely enough for probabilistic design studies.
method: PINN trained on virtual-work loss over the finite-element mesh for incremental strength reduction.
Learns many random spatial fields at once on GPU without labeled FEM solutions.
Neural operator trained on PINN-generated data to predict factor of safety, displacement path, and failure mode.
evidence_signal: Against Abaqus on 52 random fields, the PINN matched factor of safety within 2–3% RMS and identified the same weak-zone failure mechanism; reliability methods agreed down to 10^-3.
watch_item: The plastic strain band is under-resolved and even small factor-of-safety scatter can amplify tail failure probabilities, so results are mesh-dependent and need careful verification.
paper_title: Label-free physics-informed strength reduction and a neural operator for the reliability of spatially variable slopes
